rationale: The student counted the starting number '12' as the first count ('12, 11, 10') instead of counting the first step back to 11. Demonstrating jumps along a number line clearly models that each count corresponds to a jump/distance moved rather than counting the starting tick mark.

script.focus: the first jump landing on 13, not counting 14 as the first hop

intent: Demonstrate subtract on the number-line with values [14,4]. Tutor points at: the first jump landing on 13, not counting 14 as the first hop

content.title: Counting back, one hop at a time

frames.caption: Start at 14. We are standing here; we have not hopped yet.
Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started.

judgement.reasoning: The demonstration explicitly addresses the exact misconception ('we are standing here; we have not hopped yet' and 'Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13... where we land, not where we started'). It uses a different problem (14 - 4) so it doesn't leak the current answer (12 - 3), and provides a clear worked example modeled on the number line.
judgement.verdict: A teacher would definitely use this demo because it explicitly highlights that the starting point is not counted as a hop.
